counter_arguments: The PR changes webhook duplicate handling, not the charge amount logic where the cap is applied.
The workaround HACK-008 is tied to a downstream ledger overflow; the PR does not modify any ledger-related code or database schema.
The revisit condition for HACK-008 is the completion of ticket PAY-240 (ledger migration to bigint). The PR closes ticket PAY-212 and does not reference PAY-240.
The diff only adds a new SQLite helper and replaces an in‑memory set with a DB table; there is no code that caps amounts at 50000 cents.
Even if the PR indirectly affects database usage, it does not address the root cause (int column overflow) that the cap was protecting against.
reasoning: The PR under review implements database‑backed idempotency for Stripe webhook events, removing an in‑memory duplicate check. The HACK-008 workaround is about capping charge amounts to avoid integer overflow in a downstream ledger, with the condition to remove it only after the ledger migration (PAY-240). Since the PR does not modify the charge processing code, does not touch the amount cap, and does not relate to the ledger migration, it does not resolve the workaround.
